description: Parley layer-3 interop suite (docs/testing.md §layer-3). Language-neutral. Every peer is a GENERIC interpreter of this file and holds ZERO suite logic: the commander role runs the step model below; the handler role serves the five fixed HARNESS command behaviours (echo/slow/err/cancelme/busy1). Sequencing lives ONLY in this data — MQTT per-topic ordering plus the awaitProgress barrier make every scenario sleep-free and deterministic.

config._note: Suite-wide, §8-ratio-valid, compressed so the full serial matrix stays at minutes while every window keeps a >1000x margin over sub-millisecond localhost RTT. Durations are milliseconds; each peer converts to its native unit (C++/JS ms, C# TimeSpan, Python seconds). noAckTimeout=5x requestRetryInterval (§8 SHOULD 3-5x); staleTimeout=3.75x heartbeatInterval (§8 SHOULD >=3x).

harness._note: Fixed handler behaviours, keyed by command type (docs/testing.md standard command table). Parameters are read from each request's `p`. QoS 0 everywhere (protocol baseline).
harness.echo: returns the request payload as the success result (codec fidelity).
harness.slow: runs for p.durationMs, emitting a `prg` at execution start and then every p.progressEveryMs, then succeeds (heartbeats, progress, no false $executionStale).
harness.err: fails immediately with the custom error code p.code.
harness.cancelme: emits a `prg` at execution start and keeps emitting every p.progressEveryMs while parked (the barrier tolerates a lost prg) until cancelled, then completes cancelled ($cancelled).
harness.busy1: identical execution behaviour to cancelme, but its handler is constructed with maxActiveCommands=1 so a second concurrent admission yields a stateless $busy.

timeouts._note: Interpreter caps (ms). The barrier and per-call caps FAIL the scenario if exceeded; run-matrix.sh additionally enforces a per-pair wall-clock timeout so no broken peer can hang the matrix.

stepModel._note: Each step is an object with exactly one directive key. `call` fires and awaits inline with an inline `expect`. `callAsync` fires a named call WITHOUT awaiting. `awaitProgress` blocks until >=1 `prg` for a named call (THE barrier); it FAILS if the named call reaches a terminal outcome first or the cap expires. `cancel` cancels a named call. `await` awaits a named call with an `expect`. `expect` = { ok, e?, p? (deep-equal), minProgress? }.

scenarios.name: echo
scenarios.description: Happy path + codec fidelity: unicode (accents, middot, CJK, Greek, emoji), floats (3.14 exact), negatives, integers, zero, booleans, JSON null-as-value, nesting, and mixed arrays all round-trip byte-for-value.

scenarios.name: slow
scenarios.description: A scripted-duration command: terminal success within the cap and minProgress asserted. Progress here IS a sign of life — each prg (every 300 ms) resets the commander's sliding sign-of-life window (300 ms < staleTimeout 1500 ms), so the absence of $executionStale follows from the PROGRESS cadence, not from heartbeats. Heartbeat-only liveness (a progress-free window sustained by hb alone) is proven separately by the silent-slow scenario.

scenarios.name: err
scenarios.description: Custom error result: the handler fails with a consumer-typed error code, surfaced verbatim to the commander.

scenarios.name: cancelme
scenarios.description: Wire-level cancel of an EXECUTING command. callAsync + the awaitProgress barrier remove every sleep: the barrier proves admission+execution before the cancel, and MQTT per-topic ordering makes the terminal deterministic.

scenarios.name: busy1
scenarios.description: Stateless $busy on a full pool (maxActiveCommands=1). The barrier parks call `a` in the one slot before `b` is offered, so `b`'s $busy is deterministic; then `a` is cancelled.

scenarios.name: concurrent
scenarios.description: Commander-side multi-in-flight + handler FIFO queue. Two slow calls (a, b) are fired via callAsync onto the SAME slow command (one handler, maxConcurrentExecutions PINNED at 1), so the handler admits both (heartbeats flow for the queued one) but executes them one at a time FIFO — a runs, then b. Meanwhile echo call c is offered on its own command and completes independently. All three reach terminal success. maxConcurrentExecutions stays 1 by design: the loop-based harness handlers hold a single execution, so raising it would break C++ only and masquerade as a library bug.

scenarios.name: churn
scenarios.description: Command-id churn + tombstone turnover under real broker timing: 20 sequential echo calls, each admitted, completed, rak'd and tombstoned before the next is offered. Exercises id generation, per-id tombstone lifecycle, and steady-state resource reuse across many terminal outcomes (all within the default tombstone table cap).

scenarios.name: boundary-echo
scenarios.description: Near-cap codec fidelity. A unicode-mixed payload whose SERIALIZED success-res envelope sits just under the C++ peer's kMaxPayload cap (1024 B). MEASURED serialized `res` sizes for this exact payload (22-char id): 1005 B when non-ASCII is \uXXXX-escaped (C#'s System.Text.Json — the largest-serializing peer, hence the binding case whenever cpp is commander or handler) and 947 B raw-UTF-8 (JS / Python / C++). Both are < 1024 B with margin; the `req` envelope is ~10 B smaller than the `res`. Proves every codec round-trips a near-cap payload byte-for-value over the wire. Cap-EXCEEDING payloads (local reject) stay a layer-1 concern and are NOT exercised here.

scenarios.name: silent-slow
scenarios.description: Heartbeat-only liveness over the wire. durationMs == progressEveryMs == 4000 yields an entry prg then a SINGLE 4000 ms window with no progress at all — only heartbeats (every 400 ms) flow. That silent window (4000 ms) far exceeds staleTimeout (1500 ms), so the call can succeed ONLY if heartbeats alone keep resetting the commander's sliding sign-of-life window. This isolates heartbeat liveness from progress liveness (the base slow scenario proves the latter). IMPORTANT: durationMs == progressEveryMs is the ONLY cross-language-consistent silent encoding — every harness handler sleeps progressEveryMs per loop iteration, so a sentinel form (progressEveryMs > durationMs, or 0 / negative) would hang the loop-based handlers. Sentinel encodings are therefore FORBIDDEN here. minProgress is asserted >= 1 only, never an exact count: the entry/terminal prg counts are timing- and QoS-tolerant.

selfChecks.name: noAck
selfChecks.description: Commander-local $noAck: run per-commander OUTSIDE the 4x4 matrix, against a prefix with no handler. The sign-of-life window (noAckTimeout) expires before any sign of life. Tests no pair.
